newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian oil firms seen under high interest burden.
newsitem.headline: Indian oil firms seen under high interest burden.

text.p: India's state-run oil firms will continue to experience a high interest burden in the first half of 1997/98 (April-March), a senior official of investment bank SBC Warburg's India operations said on Friday.

Interest costs of top Indian refiners Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) rose in the second half of 1996/97, Sanjoy Bhattacharyya, director of SBC Warburg's local office said.
"Interest rates have begun to head south, but the impact won't be sufficient to bring it to the level of the first half of 1996/97 (for these companies)," Bhattacharyya told reporters.
SBC Warburg said it is founding an Indian broking firm and had applied for membership of the National Stock Exchange.
Company officials were speaking to reporters at the launch of its research study on India's downstream oil sector.
"SBC Warburg believes that deregulation of India's downstream oil industry is inevitable, although unlikely before the end of the century," the firm said in a statement.
It recommended investment in HPCL and BPCL.

Officials said that SBC Warburg did not include Indian Oil Coporation, India's biggest oil refiner, in its study as the investment bank is part of a syndicate working on an international capital issue planned by the Indian firm.
